correctness.rationale: Exact Jordan convolution and finite squares were recomputed. The local convolution prime-power factors give an absolute Euler norm for every \(\sigma>1/2\), proving a uniform coprimality mean. Partial summation provides the weighted mean with exponent \(\beta-1+\sigma\). Truncating quotient blocks and optimizing Q yields the three error regimes; the omitted positive tail is bounded by an integral. Absolute c_s convergence and positivity use the squared mean and \(H_q^2\). The large-s formula follows from isolating \(q=1\). The exact finite checker returns 105 rational and 12 floating checks; the infinite proof is separate.

originality.rationale: The primary source (full HTML sections 1--6) states only the fixed exponent s=2. Its s=2 asymptotic does not imply the claims for s≠2, the parameter-dependent remainder regimes or the large-s constant. The nearest indexed GCD-square result has a unimodular completely multiplicative vector, which cannot include Möbius. The standard spectral norm literature has a different denominator and proves bounds rather than a Möbius-vector asymptotic. Targeted exact, alias and broader searches showed no dominating match, but mathematical novelty is subject to unindexed coverage risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed general weighted-GCD-kernel theorem might imply the parameter family.
The three displayed error regimes are upper bounds from truncation, not optimality statements.

value.rationale: The object is the fixed-denominator family of Möbius vectors evaluated on the natural positive-semidefinite power-GCD kernels. The problem asks how the exponent controls growth, not a renamed finite calculation: the growth scale changes continuously to \(N^{s-1}\), the coefficient is explicit and strictly positive for every real \(s>1\), and the effective error changes regimes at \(\beta=1/2\) and \(\beta=3/2\). This supplies a parameter-wide asymptotic and a large-power limiting law beyond the isolated quadratic kernel, useful for interpolating GCD-kernel statistics. The error exponents are not asserted sharp and the critical endpoint remains outside scope.
